event: Thursday of week four: rain on the window of 15, and Bea asleep with her face in your neck.
You lie still and listen; Bea wakes, groans at the rain, and pulls the blanket over both heads.
"Five more minutes," she says, and kisses your collarbone, and falls straight back to sleep.
At breakfast Yusra comes through the kitchen with her glasses on and a book under her arm.
She looks rested. "Slept again," she says as she passes, only to you, and you grin into your tea.

memory.fact: At breakfast Yusra said Slept again, low, only to Nala, as she passed.

event: Morning: History of Magic in the lecture hall; the lecturer chalks a date on the board: 1858.
The Healers Act, she says: the year a healer first had to pass an examination to be licensed.

memory.fact: History's fourth week covers the Healers Act of 1858, which first licensed healers by examination.

event: Amara asks who set the first examination; the lecturer says the colleges, together, and argued.

event: You think of Yusra in the library at midnight with four books open. You write the date down twice.
After, in the corridor, Kit says the Act was the first time the colleges had to prove anything.
"Before that, it was just who your grandmother was," Kit says. "After, it was what you could do."

memory.fact: Kit said 1858 made the colleges prove things: after, it was what you could do; she likes after.

event: Bea raises her eyebrows at you across the table. You raise yours back. Lin hides a smile.
Shiv sits down in Priya's empty seat with a plate of soup and wet hair from the dawn swim.
"Sunday," Shiv says. "The rock. You're still coming?" You say yes, rain or not. She nods, pleased.

memory.fact: Nala told Shiv she's still coming to the rock on Sunday, rain or not; Shiv was pleased.

event: Afternoon: you read your essay over once more in the Snug, by the iron grate, on a green sofa.
Kit comes up the short stair with two mugs of tea and sits on the other end of the sofa.
She reads your essay with her feet tucked under her. When she's finished she's quiet a while.
"The hurt kept in while it mends," Kit says. "That's good, Nala. That's really good."

memory.fact: Kit read Nala's ward essay in the Snug and said, with no edge at all: That's really good.

event: You ask to read hers. It's about the warded door of her grandmother's house; Kit blushes.
You read it twice; you tell her it's the best thing she's written, and her ears go scarlet again.

memory.fact: Kit's essay is on the warded door of her grandmother's house; Nala called it her best yet.

event: She leans her shoulder into yours, there on the sofa, in the empty Snug, and leaves it there.
You kiss her, softly, once, by the fire; Kit kisses back, and laughs, and says "Rain."

memory.fact: Nala kissed Kit softly by the Snug fire; Kit kissed back, laughed, and said: Rain.
Nala kissed Kit softly by the Snug fire; Kit kissed back, laughed, and said: Rain.

event: At five you find Yusra in the Thornfield kitchen, making a sandwich for the night shift.
You tell her about the lecture: the Healers Act, 1858, the first examination.
Yusra stops buttering. "That's mine," she says. "The exam I'm working for. Then I'm licensed."

memory.fact: Told of the Healers Act, Yusra said: That's mine, the exam I'm working for; then I'm licensed.
Told of the Healers Act, Yusra said: That's mine, the exam I'm working for; then I'm licensed.

event: "Hands that make things better," you say. She looks at you. "You remember everything," she says.
"So do you," you say. Something in Yusra's face goes soft, and she looks back at the bread.

memory.fact: Yusra told Nala You remember everything; Nala said So do you, and Yusra's face went soft.
Yusra told Nala You remember everything; Nala said So do you, and Yusra's face went soft.

event: Seven: life drawing in the Drawing Room, lamps in place of the skylights, rain on the glass above.
The model tonight is a second-year from Ashcombe, clothed in a long grey shift, very calm.
You sit beside Lin with a board on your knee and charcoal, and draw for the first time.
Your first drawing is terrible; Lin looks at it and laughs, kindly, and moves your wrist.
"Look more," Lin says. "Draw less. Look at her, then let your hand go." You try again.

memory.fact: At Nala's first life drawing Lin moved her wrist and told her: Look more. Draw less.
At Nala's first life drawing Lin moved her wrist and told her: Look more. Draw less.

event: The second drawing is less terrible. The third has a shoulder in it that is nearly right.

memory.fact: Nala drew at life drawing for the first time; her third drawing had a shoulder nearly right.
Nala drew at life drawing for the first time; her third drawing had a shoulder nearly right.

event: Lin's drawings are quick and sure; she's lighter tonight, her mouth soft, her hand never still.
After, in the corridor, Lin takes a sealed envelope out of her bag, addressed in ink.
"I copied it out," she says. "Last night. Every word. In English and Cantonese both."
"Will you come with me," she says, "to post it? Now? Before I can think."
You walk with her through the rain to the post box by the porters' lodge, under one umbrella.
Lin stands in front of the box holding the envelope for a long moment, her hand shaking.
You take her other hand. Lin breathes out, and puts the letter in the slot, and lets go.
It drops. "Oh," Lin says. "Oh. I've done it." She starts to laugh and cry at once.
You hold her under the umbrella in the rain, and she laughs into your coat till she's done.
"Thank you," she says. "For holding my hand. I couldn't have." She kisses your cheek, wet.

event: Back at Thornfield, at half past nine, you fill the flask with sweet tea again.
Yusra comes down at quarter to ten; she sees the flask in your hands and stops on the stair.
"You'll spoil me," she says. "Good," you say. She takes it, and her fingers rest on yours again.

memory.fact: Given sweet tea again, Yusra said You'll spoil me; Nala said Good; her fingers rested on Nala's.
Given sweet tea again, Yusra said You'll spoil me; Nala said Good; her fingers rested on Nala's.

event: "Saturday," Yusra says, low. "I'm off. All day. If you'd walk with me. Up the fell, in the morning."
Bea trains at seven on Saturdays; you say yes, after you've waved Bea off on the water.
Yusra nods once. "Nine, then. At the front door." She almost smiles, and goes out into the rain.

memory.fact: Yusra asked Nala to walk up the fell on Saturday, her day off; nine, at the front door.
Yusra asked Nala to walk up the fell on Saturday, her day off; nine, at the front door.

event: In 15 Bea's sitting up in bed with her rowing book, and looks at you over the top of it.
"You've got a face on," she says. "A good one." You tell her Lin posted the letter. Bea whoops.
You tell her Yusra asked you to walk on Saturday. Bea looks at you a long moment, and smiles.

memory.fact: Yusra asked Nala to walk up the fell on Saturday, her day off; nine, at the front door.

event: "She's lonely," Bea says. "I've seen it. Go. Just come and watch me row first." You promise.

memory.fact: Told Yusra asked Nala to walk, Bea said she's lonely, go, but watch me row first; Nala promised.
Told Yusra asked Nala to walk, Bea said she's lonely, go, but watch me row first; Nala promised.

event: Bea puts her book down and pulls you in; you fall asleep with her heart going under your ear.
